instructions: Read the passage and choose one answer for each question.
passage:
On Monday, Maya saw a vacancy for a part-time visitor-desk position at a community center. She wanted to learn about the role before sending an application. The notice said that the employee would help visitors find rooms and answer simple questions. Maya liked the idea because she had enjoyed helping people at a library.

Maya spoke to her former colleague, Lina, about her experience. At the library, they had worked as a team during a busy reading event. Maya explained that her strongest skill was listening carefully when someone asked for help. Lina remembered that Maya was reliable: she arrived on time and checked her work before leaving. This gave Maya a useful example to describe to the employer.

On Tuesday, Maya completed the application and listed a certificate from a basic computer course. The notice mentioned the course as a useful qualification, but it did not say that the certificate was required. Maya did not claim to have a qualification she had not earned. She wanted an opportunity to learn more, and her longer-term career goal was to work in community education.

The next morning, the center invited her to an interview with the manager of its visitor department. Maya brought the notice and a copy of her application. The manager asked each candidate to explain how they would respond if a customer could not find a room. Maya said she would listen, check the room list and ask a colleague when she was unsure. She also asked which task a new worker would learn first.

During the conversation, the manager described the service and explained one responsibility: helping people find accurate information. The visitor desk was run with support from a local company, whose main business was organizing community events. The manager said the part-time role paid an hourly wage of twelve pounds. A monthly salary appeared in a separate notice for a different, full-time role. Maya wrote down the difference and planned to ask about working hours before making any decision.

Maya did not receive a job offer at the interview. The manager said the center would contact candidates the following week. Maya felt successful in explaining her own example clearly, even though she did not yet know the result. On Thursday she planned to resume her library volunteering. Here resume means begin again; it is a verb, not the name of a job document. The profession interested her, so she kept the notes and thought about what she wanted to improve for the next conversation.
